verses.118:1: Bem-aventurados {immaculati} no caminho: * os que andam na lei do Senhor.
verses.118:2: Bem-aventurados os que {scrutantur} {t_ejus}: * de todo o coração o {ex_3pl}.
verses.118:3: Pois os que praticam a iniquidade, * não andaram nos seus caminhos.
verses.118:5: Oxalá se dirijam os meus caminhos, * para guardar {j_acc}!
verses.118:7: Eu vos darei graças na retidão do coração: * {in_eo_quod} {jd_bare} da vossa justiça.
verses.118:8: Guardarei {j_acc}: * não me abandoneis de todo.
verses.118:9: {in_quo_a} corrige o jovem o seu caminho? * {in_quo_b} {s_acc}.
verses.118:10: De todo o meu coração vos {ex_1sg}: * não me {repellas} {m_de}.
verses.118:11: No meu coração escondi {e_acc}: * para não pecar contra vós.
verses.118:13: Com os meus lábios, * pronunciei {jd_all} da vossa boca.
verses.118:14: No caminho {t_gen} me deleitei, * como em todas as riquezas.
verses.118:18: {revela}: * e considerarei as maravilhas da vossa lei.
verses.118:19: Eu sou {incola} na terra: * não escondais de mim {m_acc}.
verses.118:20: A minha alma {concupivit} desejar {j_acc}, * em todo tempo.
verses.118:21: Repreendestes os soberbos: * malditos os que se apartam {m_de}.
verses.118:22: Tirai de mim {opprobrium} e o desprezo: * porque {ex_1sg} {t_acc}.
verses.118:23: Pois os príncipes sentaram-se, e falavam contra mim: * o vosso servo, porém, {exerc_impf} {j_in}.
verses.118:24: Pois também {t_acc} são a minha meditação: * e o meu conselho, {j_acc}.
verses.118:25: A minha alma {adh_3} {pavimento}: * {vivifica} segundo a vossa palavra.
verses.118:28: A minha alma dormitou {taedio}: * {confirma} nas vossas palavras.

decisions.latin: justificatiónes tuas · in justificatiónibus tuis · justificatiónum tuárum
decisions.why: The hard word of the psalm: 29 times here (9 of them in these 32 verses) and once in all the rest of the psalter (104:45); δικαιώματα. Lewis & Short give its biblical sense as '(as if from justa-facio) due formality' — an ordinance, a thing laid down as right to do. The Portuguese cognate does not have that sense. The full argument, the counts and the candidates are in words/ps118-terms.md §5; this one decision switches the term through the whole portion.

options.label: preceitos
options.note: Ruled (Claude, for review). Three syllables, paroxytone, native with every verb the psalm gives the word (guardar, ensinar, aprender, meditar, cumprir, cantar). Matos Soares 1932 has it 9 times for this term; Portuguese Bibles call the same Greek pair in Luke 1:6 'mandamentos e preceitos do Senhor' (fetched; Protestant editions — Catholic ones unverified). Cost: it is the cognate of præcéptum, which never occurs in Ps 118 (8 places elsewhere, always singular, mostly πρόσταγμα) and is proposed as 'decreto' in the glossary. It is also 4 syllables shorter than the Latin word, so every colon that holds it runs short by the checker.

options.label: decretos
options.note: The Diurnal Monástico's word for the matching Hebrew term (23 times): proven sayable in a Brazilian choir; collides with nothing in the Latin psalter; Matos Soares has 'justos decretos' 5 times. Against: in Brazil a decreto is first an act of government, and God's 'decretos' are his sovereign decisions rather than rules one keeps and learns. Choosing it sends præcéptum back to 'preceito'.

options.label: justificações
options.note: The cognate, and Douay-Rheims' policy ('justifications', 29 of 29). The reader crossing from the Latin column finds the same word, and the colon lengths come right. Refused as the text: in Portuguese it means excuses, proofs, or the act of being made just — 'ensinai-me as vossas justificações' is heard as 'teach me your reasons'. It would need the footnote rule 5 forbids; Matos Soares, translating this very Latin, never once uses it.

decisions.latin: testimónia ejus / tua · testimoniórum tuórum · testimóniis tuis
decisions.why: μαρτύρια, always; 22 times in the psalm. Lewis & Short: witness, attestation — nothing of the law-code in the word itself. Douay-Rheims holds 'testimonies' 22 of 22; Matos Soares scatters it over six words (testemunhos 6, preceitos 6, mandamentos 5 …).

options.label: testemunhos
options.note: Glossary, confirmed by the study. The cognate, paroxytone; heard as 'what you have attested', which is what the Latin says.

options.label: preceitos
options.note: The Diurnal Monástico's commonest word here (from the Hebrew). Only possible if 'justificationes' is moved off 'preceitos' first — otherwise two Latin terms become one. It is another word's meaning (rule 2); listed because a Brazilian ear trained on Hebrew-family psalters expects it.

decisions.latin: mandáta tua · in (ómnibus) mandátis tuis · a mandátis tuis · mandatórum tuórum
decisions.why: ἐντολαί, always; the psalm's commonest law-word (38 times, 7 of them here). The only cost of the glossary word is length: 'os vossos mandamentos' is 8 syllables for the 5 of 'mandáta tua', and it pushes several cola over the Latin's count.

options.label: mandamentos
options.note: Glossary, confirmed. The cognate; Douay-Rheims 'commandments' 34 of 38, Matos Soares 'mandamentos' about 30 of 38. It alone lets 118:4 keep its play (mandastes … mandamentos).

options.label: preceitos
options.note: The Diurnal Monástico has it 15 times beside 'mandamentos' 21 (from the Hebrew, which has two terms where the Latin has one). A syllable shorter. Only possible if 'justificationes' is moved off 'preceitos'; and 118:4 loses its echo.

decisions.latin: judícia justítiæ tuæ · ómnia judícia oris tui · judícia tua
decisions.why: κρίματα; 23 times in the psalm, 66 in the psalter. The word must also serve the singular (118:84 fácies judícium, 118:121 Feci judícium et justítiam, 118:137 rectum judícium tuum).

options.label: juízos
options.note: Glossary, confirmed. Matos Soares' commonest word for it (14), Douay-Rheims 'judgments' 21 of 23. Serves singular and plural, God's judging and his rulings. Cost: in Brazil 'juízo' is also good sense.

options.label: sentenças
options.note: The Diurnal Monástico's word (10 times). Clear for the plural — what a judge hands down — and 'as sentenças da vossa boca' (118:13) is good. It cannot serve most of judícium's other 60 places, so the Latin's one term would become two.

decisions.why: sermo is λόγος, the same Greek word as verbum: the distinction is the Latin translator's own (118:42 has verbum … sermónibus for λόγον … λόγους). Rule 1 keeps it. Five times in the psalm, always plural; 14 times elsewhere, often of a man's talk (54:22 Mollíti sunt sermónes ejus super óleum; 138:4 non est sermo in lingua mea). Lewis & Short: talk, conversation, ordinary speech. 118:16 and 118:17 both end on it, and so they do here.

options.label: falas
options.note: Ruled (Claude, for review). The exact sense of sermo, and native wherever it was tried: 'as suas falas são mais macias que o azeite' (54:22), 'não há fala na minha língua' (138:4), 'veloz corre a sua fala' (147:4). Two syllables, paroxytone. Cost: said of God's words that one keeps and does not forget, 'as vossas falas' is unusual in prayer — nobody has prayed it before.

options.label: palavras
options.note: What Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal Monástico all did, and what the Greek says. It makes verbum and sermo one word: harmless in these three verses, but 118:42 (verbum … sermónibus), 55:11 and 102:20 set the two side by side, and 118:28 'in verbis tuis' → 'nas vossas palavras' is eleven verses away.

options.label: ditos
options.note: Possible only if 'eloquia' is moved off 'ditos' (to 'promessas' or 'falas').

decisions.why: elóquium is λόγιον — an utterance, an oracle — against λόγος: this is the distinction that goes back through the Greek. 20 times in the psalm (once in these verses), 8 elsewhere, and twice there it is a man's (18:15a elóquia oris mei, 103:34 elóquium meum). Lewis & Short: 'in late Latin, declaration, communication in general'. The least certain ruling of the term set; see words/ps118-terms.md §5.

options.label: ditos
options.note: Ruled (Claude, for review). A thing uttered, God's or a man's, with a good plural: 'os ditos do Senhor são ditos puros' (11:7), 'os ditos da minha boca' (18:15a), 'segundo o vosso dito' (118:41 and seven more). Paroxytone, two syllables. Cost: it is a small word ('dito popular'), and in the formula it is thinner than 'promessa'.

options.label: promessas
options.note: The Diurnal Monástico (15 of 20, from the Hebrew) and Matos Soares three times. In 'secúndum elóquium tuum' it is what the line means, and it prays well. Refused as the text: it interprets (rule 2), and it fails where the elóquium is kept or spoken — 118:67 elóquium tuum custodívi, 118:158, 118:172 — and where it is a man's. Here: 'escondi as vossas promessas para não pecar' is already a little off.

options.label: falas
options.note: Etymologically exact (é-loqui : falar). Only possible if 'sermones' is moved off 'falas'.

options.label: palavras
options.note: Douay-Rheims ('words'), Matos Soares 15 of 20. Merges λόγιον into λόγος — the one distinction of the three that the Greek itself makes — and 147:4 sets elóquium beside sermo.

decisions.why: ἄμωμοι, without blemish. The word returns at 118:80 (Fiat cor meum immaculátum) and is said of the law itself in 18:8 (Lex Dómini immaculáta). The colon is long whatever is done, because 'Bem-aventurados' (glossary) is six syllables for Beáti's three.

options.label: os imaculados
options.note: Draft. The Latin's word, which can serve 118:80 and 18:8 unchanged. Cost: in Brazil 'imaculada' belongs first to Our Lady, and the colon is 5 syllables over the Latin.

options.label: os sem mancha
options.note: Plainer and two syllables shorter; Matos Soares has 'os que se conservam sem mácula'. A prepositional phrase doing duty as a noun is a little awkward, and 118:80 'um coração sem mancha' would follow easily.

decisions.why: scrutári (ἐξερευνάω, to search out) comes five times in the psalm (118:2, 34, 69, 115, 129) and must also serve 7:10 scrutans corda et renes Deus. It has to stay apart from exquírere in the same verse.

options.label: sondam
options.note: Draft. Plain, concrete (to sound a depth), two syllables; 'Deus que sonda os corações e os rins' (7:10) is natural. The plainer of the faithful words.

options.label: perscrutam
options.note: The cognate (per-scrutári). Exact and dignified, but learned.

options.label: esquadrinham
options.note: The precise sense of scrutári — to go through a thing piece by piece — but four rugged syllables, and 'esquadrinharei' at 118:34 would be seven.

options.label: estudam
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Tames the image.

decisions.latin: exquírunt eum · exquisívi te · testimónia tua exquisívi
decisions.why: exquírere (ἐκζητέω) eight times in the psalm, beside the simple quǽrere (118:100 quæsívi, 118:176 quære servum tuum) and requírere (118:145). The glossary has quǽrere → buscar.

options.label: procurar
options.note: Draft. Keeps the compound apart from quǽrere → buscar, so that 118:176 'buscai o vosso servo' is a different verb from the one the psalmist uses of himself eight times. 'Procurar a Deus de todo o coração' is native.

options.label: buscar
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 (sometimes 'busquei cuidadoso', to give the ex- its due); Douay-Rheims 'seek / sought after'. The more biblical verb; merges exquírere with quǽrere.

decisions.why: The verb and its own noun side by side (so the Greek: ἐνετείλω τὰς ἐντολάς). The glossary has mandáre → 'dar ordem' (open, Ps 90:11), with the note that it loses the link with mandáta; here the link is the line.

options.label: mandastes
options.note: Draft: 'Vós mandastes que os vossos mandamentos …' — the repetition is the Latin's own (D2). The glossary row for mandáre is widened accordingly.

options.label: ordenastes
options.note: Natural and clear; the echo is gone. Matos Soares has 'promulgaste'.

options.label: destes ordem
options.note: The glossary's phrase from Ps 90:11, for consistency across psalms; the echo is gone here too.

decisions.why: nimis (σφόδρα, exceedingly) qualifying 'to be kept'. It returns at 118:96 (latum mandátum tuum nimis) and 118:138, and often elsewhere (47:2 laudábilis nimis); no single Portuguese adverb sits naturally in all of them.

options.label: à risca
options.note: Draft, from Matos Soares 1932. The native intensifier for keeping a rule; paroxytone at the close. Cost: it cannot be the word at 118:96 or 118:138 — nimis will not have one rendering.

options.label: sobremaneira
options.note: The literal 'exceedingly', and it could serve 118:96 and 118:138 as well. Bookish, and 'guardar sobremaneira' is not something one says.

options.label: com todo o cuidado
options.note: Douay-Rheims 'most diligently'; the Diurnal Monástico 'com cuidado'. Supplies a noun.

decisions.why: confúndi (αἰσχύνομαι, to be put to shame) six times in the psalm, and it is the verb of 30:2 = 70:1 In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum — the last line of the Te Deum. It stands in a cluster with erubéscere and reveréri (34:4, 34:26, 39:15, 69:3–4), so the three want three words. The passive is traditional in Portuguese prayer; the active is the difficulty: 'não me confundais' is heard as 'do not muddle me'.

options.label: ser confundido
options.note: Draft. The cognate, kept in the passive participle, where its biblical sense lives; at 118:31 the active 'noli me confúndere' is turned with 'deixar' so that the participle can stay. Costs: 'deixeis' is a word the Latin does not have; the participle is masculine (a woman praying alone says 'confundida'); 118:6 runs 4 syllables over.

options.label: ser confundido / não me confundais
options.note: The active verb as the Latin has it. Shorter; risks being heard as 'do not confuse me'.

options.label: envergonhar
options.note: What the verb means, heard at once (Douay-Rheims 'put me not to shame'; the Diurnal Monástico 'não terei de envergonhar-me'). It takes the natural word of erubéscere and gives up the Te Deum's line.

decisions.latin: cum perspéxero in ómnibus mandátis tuis
decisions.why: perspícere in: to look closely into (ἐπιβλέπειν ἐπί); Douay-Rheims 'when I shall look into'. Matos Soares paraphrases ('quando me empregar atento na observância de'). consideráre (118:15, 18) is another verb and needs to stay free.

options.label: fitar
options.note: Draft. Keeps the eyes and the steadiness of per-; one word for one.

options.label: olhar para
options.note: Plainer; the per- is lost, and 'olhar' is busy elsewhere (despícere → olhar de cima).

decisions.why: ἐν τῷ μεμαθηκέναι με: 'in that I have learned' — open between the ground of the thanksgiving and its time. Douay-Rheims takes it as time ('when I shall have learned'), Matos Soares as cause ('porque aprendi').

options.label: por ter aprendido
options.note: Draft. An infinitive, as in the Greek; leans to cause but fixes no tense, so the 'when' is not shut out.

options.label: quando tiver aprendido
options.note: Douay-Rheims. Resolves to time, and to a future the Latin perfect does not say.

options.label: porque aprendi
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Resolves to cause; keeps the perfect.

decisions.why: Question and answer hang on one preposition (ἐν τίνι … ἐν τῷ φυλάσσεσθαι): by what? — by keeping. Douay-Rheims keeps it ('By what … ? by observing'); Matos Soares has 'De que modo … ? Guardando'.

options.label: Com que … ? Guardando …
options.note: Draft. 'Com que' asks for the means, as 'in quo' does; the gerund is how Portuguese answers it.

options.label: Em que … ? Em guardar …
options.note: The Latin's preposition twice. 'Em que corrige' is heard as 'in what respect', which is not the sense.

options.label: Como … ? Guardando …
options.note: The most natural question (Diurnal Monástico: 'Como, jovem, seguir caminhos puros?'); 'in quo' is no longer heard.

decisions.latin: ne repéllas me a mandátis tuis
decisions.why: 'Do not thrust me away from your commandments' (μὴ ἀπώσῃ με ἀπό). Both Vulgate versions soften it to straying (Douay-Rheims 'let me not stray', Matos Soares 'não me deixes transviar'), which is the Hebrew's sense, not the Latin's: in the Latin it is God who would do the pushing. repéllere is the verb of 42:2 quare me repulísti and 59:3 Deus, repulísti nos.

options.label: não me rejeiteis dos
options.note: Draft. 'rejeitar' is the verb those other places will want ('por que me rejeitastes?'); with 'de' it is compressed but clear. 'repelir' was refused for its forms (não me repilais).

options.label: não me afasteis dos
options.note: Smoother; but 'afastar' is amovére's verb in 118:29, in this same portion, and it is milder than a thrust.

options.label: não me deixeis desviar dos
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 and Douay-Rheims. Refused: it makes the psalmist the one who strays.

decisions.why: exercéri in: to be busied, exercised in (the Greek ἀδολεσχέω is 'to talk on, to muse'; the Latin chose its own image and is followed). Five times in the psalm, and each time next to meditári or meditátio (118:15/16, 118:23/24), so the two verbs cannot be one.

options.label: exercitar-se em
options.note: Draft. The Latin's word (Matos Soares has it at 118:15, Douay-Rheims at 118:27 'I shall be exercised'). Five syllables in the future; 118:15 runs 3 over.

options.label: ocupar-se em
options.note: Douay-Rheims at 118:23 ('was employed in'). Plainer and a syllable shorter; paler.

options.label: meditar
options.note: Matos Soares at 118:23 and 118:27, Douay-Rheims at 118:15. Refused: 118:15–16 would then say 'meditarei' twice where the Latin has two verbs.

decisions.why: retribúere (ἀνταπόδος: render, requite) belongs with retribútio → retribuição (glossary; 118:112 propter retributiónem). But the vós imperative of 'retribuir' is 'retribuí', which is also 'I repaid' — rule 3 forbids the verb at this form.

options.label: Recompensai o
options.note: Draft. One verb for one, safe under rule 3 (past 'recompensei'), and the Latin's length. retribúere is to give back what is due, and 'recompensar' is that; it leans to reward, which is the sense here (the servant asks for life). Cost: it leaves the family of retribútio → retribuição (118:112), which the verb can rejoin at every form but this one (115:3 'Que retribuirei ao Senhor?').

options.label: Dai retribuição ao
options.note: Keeps the glossary's family through the noun; 'dai' is safe (past 'dei'). Four syllables over the Latin, and an abstract noun at the head of a stanza.

options.label: Retribuí ao
options.note: The glossary verb itself. Refused: the imperative equals the first-person past (rule 3). What DO's Portuguese has now.

decisions.why: Twelve times in the psalm, nine of them the prayer 'vivífica me'. One Latin word (the Greek has ζῆσόν με; at 118:17 the Greek has a future, 'I shall live', and the Latin's imperative is followed).

options.label: vivificai-me
options.note: Draft. One word for one, the Latin's own, and the same length; safe under rule 3 (past 'vivifiquei'). It will also carry the perfects (118:50 vivificávit me, 118:93 vivificásti me). Churchly, but known from 'Espírito vivificante'.

options.label: dai-me a vida
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Plainer and warmer; supplies a noun (compare the refusal of 'oferecer sacrifício' in Ps 53:8), and 'vita' is another word.

decisions.why: re-veláre: take the veil off (ἀποκάλυψον). The glossary has revelátio → revelação, but 'revelai os meus olhos' says something else in Portuguese; and 'abri' and 'descobri' both fail rule 3.

options.label: Desvendai os meus olhos
options.note: Draft. des-vendar is re-veláre piece for piece (to take off a blindfold), one word for one, safe under rule 3 (past 'desvendei').

options.label: Tirai o véu dos meus olhos

forms.revela: Tirai o véu dos meus olhos

options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Names the veil outright; three syllables over.

decisions.why: íncola here is πάροικος, one who lives in a land that is not his. It must stay apart from peregrinátio (118:54 in loco peregrinatiónis meæ), ádvena and peregrínus (38:13) and aliénus → estranho (glossary).

options.label: forasteiro
options.note: Draft. One from elsewhere who lives here: the sense of πάροικος, plain and Brazilian.

options.label: estrangeiro
options.note: The Diurnal Monástico. Narrows it to nationality, and ádvena will want it.

options.label: peregrino
options.note: Matos Soares 1932; Douay-Rheims 'sojourner'. Beloved, but it is peregrínus' word, and 118:54 has peregrinátio.

decisions.why: A desire doubled: 'my soul has coveted to desire' (ἐπεπόθησεν τοῦ ἐπιθυμῆσαι). Douay-Rheims keeps it ('hath coveted to long for'); Matos Soares collapses it ('desejou ansiosa'). Rule 2 keeps the Latin's strangeness. concupíscere returns at 118:40 and 118:174, and in 83:3.

options.label: cobiçou desejar
options.note: Draft. The root of concupíscere (cobiça), as strong in Portuguese as in Latin, and with the same shadow (non concupísces).

options.label: ansiou por desejar
options.note: Without the shadow of sin; softer than the Latin.

decisions.why: oppróbrium (ὄνειδος, reproach) is frequent in the psalter (21:7 oppróbrium hóminum, Ps 68 five times, 118:39), so the word chosen here will travel.

options.label: o opróbrio
options.note: Draft. The cognate, and the word both Brazilian witnesses write here (Matos Soares 1932, Diurnal Monástico 1962). Literary; a blind reader may not know it.

options.label: a afronta
options.note: The plainer word for a public insult borne. exprobráre (118:42) could then be 'afrontar'.

decisions.latin: Adhǽsit paviménto ánima mea · Adhǽsi testimóniis tuis
decisions.why: One verb twice in the stanza (ἐκολλήθη / ἐκολλήθην, was glued to): the soul stuck to the floor, the man stuck to the testimonies. Rule 6 wants one Portuguese verb for both; Matos Soares has two ('prostrou-se', 'aderi'). It must also serve 62:9 Adhǽsit ánima mea post te, 21:16 lingua mea adhǽsit fáucibus meis, 72:28 mihi autem adhærére Deo bonum est.

options.label: apegar-se a
options.note: Draft. Physical and of the heart at once, as the Latin verb is; native in all the places listed ('a minha alma apegou-se a vós').

options.label: colar-se a
options.note: The Greek's image, and the Diurnal Monástico's ('está colada no pó'). Vivid at 118:25; 'colei-me aos vossos testemunhos' is odd.

options.label: aderir a
options.note: The cognate (Matos Soares at 118:31). Abstract — one adheres to a party — and wrong for a soul on the floor.

decisions.why: pavīméntum (ἔδαφος): the beaten floor, the ground. Douay-Rheims 'pavement'; Matos Soares 'por terra'; the Hebrew-family versions have 'pó' (dust), which is not the Latin's word.

options.label: chão
options.note: Draft. The concrete, everyday word for what is under one's feet.

options.label: pavimento
options.note: The cognate. In Brazil it is a road surface or the storey of a building.

decisions.latin: Vias meas … · Viam justificatiónum … · Viam iniquitátis … · Viam veritátis … · Viam mandatórum …
decisions.why: Five of the eight verses of Daleth open on Via-: the Hebrew acrostic (every line beginning with one letter) shows through the Latin as an anaphora. D2 gives order to the ear; but this order is also a repetition, which D2 keeps. One switch for the five verses.

options.label: natural order

forms.v26a: Expus os meus caminhos, e me escutastes
forms.v29a: Afastai de mim o caminho da iniquidade

options.note: Draft. 'caminho' is still heard in all five lines, only not at their head; nothing is inverted for its own sake (rule 5), and the stanza stays as plain as the other three.

options.label: 'caminho' first, as in the Latin

forms.v26a: Os meus caminhos expus, e me escutastes
forms.v29a: O caminho da iniquidade afastai de mim

options.note: The stanza's shape made visible beside the Latin column. Five object-first lines out of eight; Portuguese bears each one alone, the run of them is mannered.

decisions.why: ínstrue me with a second accusative (συνέτισόν με: make me understand). The vós imperative of 'instruir' is 'instruí', which is also 'I instructed' — rule 3. docére (118:26, the verse before) has 'ensinar'.

options.label: Fazei-me entender o caminho
options.note: Draft, with Douay-Rheims ('Make me to understand') and the Diurnal Monástico ('Faze-me entender'). It is the Greek verb exactly, whose noun is the psalm's intelléctus (da mihi intelléctum, 118:34 …). 'fazei' is safe.

options.label: Instruí-me no caminho
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ('Instrui-me no caminho', under tu). The cognate. Refused: under vós the imperative equals the first-person past (rule 3).

options.label: Ensinai-me o caminho
options.note: Plain; but it is docére's verb, and 118:26 ends 'ensinai-me os vossos preceitos'.

decisions.why: tǽdium stands for ἀκηδία — the weariness of soul the monks called acedia. (Rahlfs prints ἔσταξεν, 'dripped', for the verb; the Latin's dormitávit follows the other reading, 'grew drowsy', and is followed.) Douay-Rheims 'through heaviness'; Matos Soares 'de tédio'.

options.label: de tédio
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932. The Latin's word; today it leans to boredom — which is not far from what acedia is.

options.label: de abatimento
options.note: Nearer Douay-Rheims' 'heaviness'. Longer, and 'humílitas' later in the psalm (118:50, 92) may want it.

decisions.why: confirmáre: make firm (βεβαίωσον). It recurs (50:14 spíritu principáli confírma me) beside firmáre and fortitúdo, which want words of their own.

options.label: confirmai-me
options.note: Draft. The cognate; 'confirmar' still means to make firm in church Portuguese (the sacrament). Safe under rule 3 (past 'confirmei').

options.label: fortalecei-me
options.note: Matos Soares 1932 ('fortifica-me'), Douay-Rheims 'strengthen'. Plainer; takes the word of fortitúdo.

options.label: firmai-me
options.note: The concrete sense, shorter; it is firmáre's word.

decisions.why: 'Out of your law have mercy on me' (Douay-Rheims: 'out of thy law'); the Greek has a bare dative (τῷ νόμῳ σου ἐλέησόν με). The Latin 'de' is open: from the law as source, by it as means, according to it. Matos Soares settles on 'segundo a tua lei'.

options.label: pela vossa lei
options.note: Draft. 'por' is as open as 'de' is — by, through, for the sake of — and is natural Portuguese.

options.label: segundo a vossa lei
options.note: Matos Soares 1932. Clear; but it is the psalm's 'secúndum' (secúndum verbum tuum, four verses earlier), which the Latin did not write here.

options.label: da vossa lei
options.note: Word for word. 'e da vossa lei tende piedade de mim' is heard as 'have mercy on me from your law' — rescue me from it.

decisions.why: DECISIONS.md D8 asked that dilatáre be looked at again here (4:2a dilatásti mihi → 'me abristes espaço'). Here it has an object, the heart, and Portuguese has the expression ready-made.

options.label: dilatastes
options.note: Draft, with Matos Soares 1932. 'Dilatar o coração' is living Portuguese. It does not help 4:2a, where there is no object: dilatáre will have two renderings.

options.label: alargastes
options.note: Plainer, the Latin's 'wide' (latus) audible; 'alargar o coração' is less idiomatic.

choices.118:1: Beáti → 'Bem-aventurados' (glossary, beátus vir): six syllables for three, so both this colon and 118:2's run long (+5, +2); accepted. ámbulant → 'andam', not 'caminham', which would make an echo with 'caminho' that neither the Latin (via / ámbulant) nor the Greek has. 'os que' resumes the relative after the asterisk. The (Aleph) label is not reproduced.
choices.118:2: Two verbs of seeking in one verse, kept apart: scrutántur → 'sondam', exquírunt → 'procuram' (decisions). in toto corde → 'de todo o coração', the Portuguese idiom, set for the six places the phrase has in the psalm. The second colon has no 'qui' in the Latin and none here.
choices.118:3: Non enim qui … ambulavérunt: the negative is moved to the verb, where Portuguese wants it. enim → 'Pois' (as Ps 53:6). operári iniquitátem → 'praticar a iniquidade' (Matos Soares 1932): the phrase is frequent (qui operámini iniquitátem, 6:9 …) and this can serve it; 'obrar' was refused (archaic, and coarse in Brazil). The perfect kept: 'não andaram'. One of the six verses of the psalm with no law-word; it has via instead.
choices.118:4: mandáta … custodíri: the Latin passive infinitive becomes 'que … se guardem', which keeps 'os vossos mandamentos' right after 'mandastes' as in the Latin; 3 syllables over. An active infinitive ('guardar à risca os vossos mandamentos') would be the right length and lose the adjacency.
choices.118:5: Útinam → 'Oxalá' (Matos Soares 1932). dirigántur → 'se dirijam': dirígere returns at 118:128 and 118:133. Second colon 5 short by the checker: the whole deficit is the term (justificatiónes 7 syllables, preceitos 3) and will recur wherever the term does — 118:8, 12, 16, 20, 23, 24; accepted psalm-wide, see words/ps118-terms.md.
choices.118:6: perspéxero is a future perfect; the Portuguese future subjunctive ('quando eu fitar') is the natural tense after 'quando'. 'eu' is named because 'fitar' alone is also third person.
choices.118:7: Confitébor tibi → 'Eu vos darei graças' (D5, settled; the same wording as the glossary's 117:21). in directióne cordis → 'na retidão do coração'. judícia justítiæ tuæ → 'os juízos da vossa justiça': this phrase returns at 118:106, 160, 164 and must be identical there; 118:62 (judícia justificatiónis tuæ) is a different Latin and must not be.
choices.118:8: Object-first in the Latin; natural order here (D2). derelínquere → 'abandonar' (the verb 21:2 will want). usquequáque (ἕως σφόδρα, utterly) → 'de todo'; it returns at 118:43, 51, 107. Matos Soares' 'jamais' is another sense.
choices.118:9: adolescéntior is a comparative standing for the Greek νεώτερος, 'a young man': 'o jovem' (Matos Soares 1932, Douay-Rheims). córrigit is present in the Latin (the Greek has a future): followed. córrigit → 'corrige', the cognate; 'endireita' would be the image. The (Beth) label is not reproduced.
choices.118:11: peccem tibi, a dative → 'pecar contra vós' (grammar). ut non → 'para não' with the infinitive.
choices.118:12: 'Bendito sois, Senhor' — bare vocative (glossary). doce me justificatiónes tuas comes again word for word at 118:26 (and 118:64, 68, 124, 135 with the order changed): 'ensinai-me os vossos preceitos' is set as the formula; 'ensinai' is safe under rule 3.
choices.118:13: In lábiis meis → 'Com os meus lábios' (the instrument; Douay-Rheims 'With my lips', Matos Soares 'Com os meus lábios'). The Latin's comma before the asterisk is kept. pronuntiáre → 'pronunciar' (again at 118:172); enuntiáre in 118:26 is a different Latin verb for the same Greek one and gets a different word.
choices.118:14: delectátus sum → 'me deleitei'. 'como em todas as riquezas' word for word.
choices.118:15: First colon 3 over: 'mandamentos' and 'me exercitarei' are both longer than their Latin; accepted (see decisions 'mandata', 'exerceri').
choices.118:16: meditári → 'meditar em'. oblivísci → 'esquecer' with a direct object, as the Latin has an accusative. 118:16 and 118:17 end on the same two words in the Latin (sermónes tuos) and so here: the checker's neighbouring-finals flag is the Latin's own echo.
choices.118:17: Retríbue → 'Recompensai' (decision 'retribue': 'retribuí' fails rule 3). vivífica me is an imperative in the Latin where the Greek has 'I shall live'; the Latin is followed. The verse ends on a colon in the Latin and here. custódiam → 'guardarei' (glossary). The (Ghimel) label is not reproduced.
choices.118:18: mirabília de lege tua → 'as maravilhas da vossa lei': 'da' is both 'of' and 'from', as wide as 'de'. consideráre → 'considerar', as in 118:15.
choices.118:19: ego is expressed in the Latin and here ('Eu sou'). 'não escondais' is a subjunctive, no rule-3 risk.
choices.118:20: in omni témpore → 'em todo tempo' without the article, which in Brazil is 'at every time'. The Latin has justificatiónes where Rahlfs has κρίματα; the Latin is followed. First colon 6 short: nothing is left out — 'desideráre justificatiónes' alone is 12 syllables.
choices.118:21: increpáre → 'repreender' (Matos Soares' 'ameaçar' is another verb). declináre a → 'apartar-se de', set for 118:51, 102, 157 and 118:115 (Apartai-vos de mim, malignos); 'desviar' is kept for avértere (glossary; 118:37). 'malditos os que' without a verb, as the Latin.
choices.118:23: Étenim → 'Pois' (καὶ γάρ); 118:24's Nam et is the same Greek and is 'Pois também'. The perfect and the imperfects are kept (sentaram-se … falavam … exercitava-se). autem → 'porém', after the subject as in the Latin. Natural order in the first colon.
choices.118:24: The second colon has no verb in the Latin and none here (a comma does the work). consílium → 'conselho'. meditátio mea est comes seven more times in the psalm (118:77, 92, 97, 99, 143, 174): '… é / são a minha meditação'.
choices.118:25: secúndum verbum tuum → 'segundo a vossa palavra', the Nunc dimittis' wording (ps233), word for word; it returns at 118:65 and 118:107. The (Daleth) label is not reproduced.
choices.118:27: exercébor in mirabílibus tuis → 'me exercitarei nas vossas maravilhas', the same verb as 118:15 and 118:23.
choices.118:28: dormitáre → 'dormitar', kept apart from dormíre (120:4 non dormitábit neque dórmiet); Matos Soares' 'adormeceu' merges them. in verbis tuis → 'nas vossas palavras', the Latin's 'in' kept.
choices.118:29: amovére → 'afastar' (safe: past 'afastei'). miserére mei → 'tende piedade de mim' (formula). First colon 3 over.
choices.118:30: non sum oblítus → 'não esqueci': the phrase closes six more verses of the psalm (118:61, 83, 109, 141, 153, 176) and should be this each time.
choices.118:32: Viam … cucúrri, a plain accusative → 'Corri o caminho' (Douay-Rheims 'I have run the way'); Matos Soares' 'pelo caminho' is the option nobody needs. cum + perfect indicative → 'quando'. Second colon 3 over.

audit.note: Latin = DO Psalm118.txt, 176 prayed verses, each with one '*' and no other mark; this file holds 118:1–118:32 only (stanzas Aleph–Daleth, the portion of Sunday Prime) and later agents append. The Hetzenauer 1914 print read of the Latin was skipped overnight and is owed.

Before any verse: words/ps118-terms.md — the law-vocabulary counted from the Latin (ps118/terms.py → terms.md), the Greek behind each term, Lewis & Short, what Douay-Rheims, Matos Soares 1932 and the Diurnal Monástico did (ps118/renderings.py → renderings.md), and a ruling under the night's delegation: lex → lei, testimónia → testemunhos, mandáta → mandamentos, justificatiónes → preceitos, judícia → juízos, verbum → palavra, sermo → fala, elóquium → dito, via → caminho, sémita → vereda. Each term with a live alternative is one multi-slot glossary decision here. ps118/verbs.py lists the recurring verbs; ps118/concordances.sh regenerates the words/ concordances; ps118/cnbb_tally.py is diction evidence only.

Stanza-level draft from consult/parallels/ps118.md. DO's Portuguese was not used as evidence (D12). Latin against the Greek, Latin followed: 118:9 córrigit present (Greek future); 118:17 vivífica me imperative (Greek 'I shall live'); 118:20 justificatiónes (Greek κρίματα); 118:28 dormitávit (Rahlfs ἔσταξεν). Rule 3 checked at every imperative: ensinai, dai, vivificai, desvendai, tirai, fazei, confirmai, afastai, tende are safe; 'retribuí' (118:17) and 'instruí' (118:27) fail and were recast. Register held plain on purpose: no variation added to the Latin's own.

PARTIAL hard check. checks.py cannot run on a partial psalm (it stops at the first untranslated verse), so ps118/partial.py runs checks.py's own code, unchanged, with the Latin restricted to the verses translated, after confirming that the 32 ids are an unbroken run of DO's ids from 118:1 in DO's order; 118:33–118:176 are missing, as expected. For the 32 verses: ids and marks match (one '*' each, nothing else). Soft flags, all accepted: six cola run 3–6 short and every one of them holds 'preceitos' (3 syllables for the 7 of justificatiónes: 118:5, 8, 16, 20, 23, 24) — the price of the term, psalm-wide; six run 3–5 long: 118:1 (Bem-aventurados, glossary), 118:4 (mandamentos + the passive clause), 118:6 (não serei confundido), 118:15 (mandamentos + me exercitarei), 118:29, 118:32 (quando dilatastes o meu coração) — nothing is added in any of them. Neighbouring finals: 118:16/17 (falas / falas) and 118:23/24 (preceitos / preceitos) are the Latin's own repetitions (sermónes tuos twice; justificatiónibus tuis / justificatiónes tuæ). No rhyme inside a verse, no cadence flag. A first run showed a doubled 'aos aos' in 118:31 from two overlapping slots, and 118:17 at +4 with 'Dai retribuição ao'; both mended before any reader saw the text.
